extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of comparative government and constitutional design (educated public, policymakers, historians)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting normative criteria and standards for evaluating constitutions, republics, and monarchies (balance of powers, representation, elections, judicial and executive structures) based on historical examples and political theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable representation in the lower house
rubrics_metrics.description: If the people are not equitably represented in the house of commons, this is a departure in practice from the theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text treats equitable representation as a fundamental requirement: lack of fair representation undermines the constitution's theoretical balance and produces practical departures from intended limits on other powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: No overlap between upper and lower houses (avoid lords returning members)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the lords return members of the house of commons, this is an additional disturbance of the balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holding the same persons or interests in both chambers corrupts bicameral balance and undermines the distinct checks intended between estates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive negative (veto) as a balancing mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: The Americans have not indeed imitated it in giving a negative, upon their legislature to the executive power; in this respect their balances are incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An executive negative (veto) is presented as a necessary component of a complete system of checks and balances; its absence leaves the system vulnerable to instability.

rubrics_metrics.name: System of balances to adjust power and prevent its vibrations
rubrics_metrics.description: The English constitution is ... the most stupendous fabric of human invention, both for the adjustment of the balance, and the prevention of its vibrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A constitution should provide multiple mechanisms to adjust competing powers and dampen sudden swings (vibrations) that would destabilize government; this is praised as a major civic art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal, constitutional, and peaceful modes for changing rulers
rubrics_metrics.description: It is absolutely necessary, to avoid continual violence, to give the people a legal, constitutional, and peaceable mode of changing these rulers, whenever they discover improper principles or dispositions in them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing lawful mechanisms for removal or replacement of rulers prevents recurring violent upheavals; necessary especially where property and political power are broadly distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of property as a criterion for constitutional design
rubrics_metrics.description: In future ages, if the present states become great nations, rich, powerful, and luxurious, as well as numerous, their own feelings and good sense will dictate to them what to do: they may make transitions to a nearer resemblance of the British constitution ... But this will never become necessary, until great quantities of property shall get into few hands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The social distribution of property affects what constitutional arrangements are appropriate: widely distributed property supports republican mechanisms; concentrated property pushes toward aristocratic/monarchical adaptations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of a mediating power of the people between king and nobles
rubrics_metrics.description: There being no mediating power of the people, collectively or representatively, between them, the consequence has been ... confusion and calamity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A representative or collective people acting as a mediating force prevents nobles from usurping executive power and preserves public order; absence of this mediating power leads to oligarchic domination and disorder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unanimity rules (liberum veto); use majority decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: The liberum veto, or the power of each nuncio to interpose a negative, and break up a diet ... gave unlimited scope to faction ... In consequence of this necessity of unanimity ... Poland has continued above a hundred years almost without laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision rules requiring unanimity or allowing a single member to break proceedings produce paralysis and lawlessness; majority rule or qualified majorities are necessary to avoid factional blockade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent foreign interference and corruption of representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal cause of all were the foreign powers, interested to foment confusions in the Polish councils ... they might put an end to any diet, unfriendly to their views, by corrupting a single member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguards are needed to prevent bribery, foreign influence, and the corruption of individual deputies, because external powers can exploit weak decision rules to control domestic outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability of high officers; avoid life appointments without effective oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The great officers of state ... being once nominated by the king, enjoyed their offices for life, responsible only to the diets, conscious that they could at all times engage a nuncio to protest, and thus elude an enquiry into their administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Life tenure without practical oversight allows officeholders to evade scrutiny; constitutions should provide mechanisms for accountability, removal, or inquiry to prevent misuse of power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of powers into three independent branches
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be laid down as a universal maxim, that every government that has not three independent branches in its legislature will soon become an absolute monarchy; or, an arrogant nobility ... will annihilate the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An institutional equilibrium among three independent branches (interpreted here as a balance among estates/branches) is essential to prevent concentration of power in a monarch or oligarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict execution and enforcement of laws
rubrics_metrics.description: A free republic is the bed of governments ... A free republic consists in the strict execution of its laws, and an equilibrium of estates or orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws must not merely exist; they must be strictly and impartially enforced. Weak enforcement undermines liberty and produces oligarchy or despotism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent venality and monetary purchase of office or crown
rubrics_metrics.description: Every succeeding king ... has always been constrained to purchase the crown by a public largess, and private corruption. Such is Polish liberty, and such the blessings of a monarchy elective by a body of nobles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elective mechanisms that permit bribery, public largess, or purchase of office corrupt legitimacy; constitutions should minimize monetary influence in selection of rulers or representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include and admit lower orders/commonalty into administration
rubrics_metrics.description: The nobility ... never permit strangers, or the commonalty, to have any participation: they elect their king, and would never suffer the senate to make themselves roasters of this election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusion of commoners from participation enables oligarchy and social oppression; inclusion of broader orders in administration helps balance elite power and protect general welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial centralization and right of appeal (avoid nobles' courts without appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: It was enacted that ... each palatinate shall elect in their dietines their own judges, who shall form supreme courts of justice, called tribunalia regni, in which the causes of the nobles shall be decided without appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating localized or privileged courts that decide nobles' causes without appeal undermines equality before the law; a unified, impartial judiciary with appeals is necessary to protect rights and prevent oligarchic impunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid concentrating executive power in a permanent council without checks
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive power is now vested in the supreme permanent council; but here neither have they any checks, all being decided by the majority, and the same principal families will always prevail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permanent executive bodies that operate by majorities dominated by elite families can entrench oligarchy; executive structures require external checks and broader representation to be legitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular convocation of representative assemblies
rubrics_metrics.description: That the diets, the holding of which depended solely upon the will of the kings, should be assembled every two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predictable, regular meetings of representative bodies are important for accountability and for preventing rulers or elites from obstructing legislative oversight by withholding assemblies.
